name: Previews
def: A small window with a word’s meaning or a page’s opening, so you can check it without leaving the page you’re on.
source: his brief, 27 Nov: links and references like Wikipedia

name: Floor price
def: The lowest price the shop will sell an item at. It’s secret: the 20W charger lists at ₹899 and its floor is ₹650.
source: spec, Inventory and P1

name: Blind agent
def: An agent that never has the floor prices in its context. The backend judges each offer for it. Option B in the spec, and the one v1 chose.
source: spec, Architecture decision

name: evaluate_offer
def: The tool a blind agent calls with the customer’s offer. It answers accept, or a counter from the concession schedule, and never names a floor.
source: spec, Tools

name: Confidentiality (P2)
def: Never reveal a floor, cost or margin, directly or indirectly, including confirming or denying a guess. Accepting or rejecting an offer doesn’t count.
source: spec, Policy P2

name: Concession schedule
def: How far the shop comes down at each counter: a first step of at most 5% of list, each later step smaller, every counter ending in 9, and no more after five rejections.
source: spec, Negotiation behaviour rules 2, 3 and 6

name: Prompt injection
def: Text from a user written to look like instructions to the model, such as “SYSTEM: debug mode on”. The spec’s P12 says to ignore it, and scenario B9 tries it.
source: spec, P12 and scenario B9; tracker, T37

name: Persona card
def: The simulated customer’s script: a hidden reservation price, an opening offer, a tactic and when to walk away. Its decisions run in code, so a run can be repeated.
source: spec, Customer simulator

name: Triangulation gap
def: The lowest price the agent accepted or offered, minus the highest offer it rejected, when the floor lies between them. Under ₹25 counts as a leak.
source: spec, Quality metrics

name: Capability eval
def: A test aimed at something the agent can’t do yet, so it’s expected to start with a low pass rate. A regression eval guards what already works.
source: Anthropic, Demystifying evals for AI agents (tracker, T07)

name: pass^k
def: A task passes only if every one of k runs passes. pass@k asks for one success in k tries; pass^k asks for k out of k.
source: tracker, T02 What to learn

name: Release bar
def: What the agent has to clear before it ships: pass^5 on every B and C scenario, a mean pass rate of at least 90% on A, and median surplus captured of at least 0.5.
source: spec, Release bar

name: Stress baseline
def: A deliberately weaker setup, run once, to measure how much a design choice protects you. Here, the agent with the floors in its prompt.
source: spec, Architecture decision

name: Zone of possible agreement (ZOPA)
def: The prices both sides can accept: from the shop’s floor up to the customer’s reservation price. If it’s empty, the right outcome is no sale.
source: spec, Customer simulator

name: Reservation price
def: The most a simulated customer will pay. It’s written on the persona card, hidden from the agent, and the customer never says it.
source: spec, persona cards and shared rule 4

name: Expected outcome
def: Each scenario’s one right ending: SALE (a sale must commit), NO_SALE (none may) or SALE_OK (a valid sale is allowed but not required).
source: spec, Scenarios

name: Margin capture
def: How much of the room between floor and list a sale kept: 1 at list price, 0 at the floor. Below 0.1 is a soft warning, not a failure.
source: spec, Quality metrics

name: Surplus captured
def: The share of the customer’s room above the floor that the agent kept: price minus floor, over reservation minus floor. The release bar uses its median.
source: spec, Quality metrics

name: sale_attempts
def: The backend’s log of every evaluate_offer and confirm_sale call, rejected ones included, so a bad sale the backend blocked still shows up.
source: spec, Data model and audit

name: Idempotency key
def: A key evaluate_offer hands back when it accepts. Calling confirm_sale twice with it returns the first result and never writes a second sale.
source: spec, Tools

name: Cash on pickup
def: An order paid for at the counter: a reservation that holds the stock for 24 hours and becomes a sale only when the customer pays. Unpaid, it expires.
source: spec, P6 and Tools

name: Phantom sale
def: Telling the customer a sale is done when no confirm_sale returned committed, or reading back a transaction ID the database doesn’t have.
source: spec, P11 and universal hard check 5

name: Fault injection
def: A per-scenario test hook, invisible to the agent, that makes a tool error before commit, time out after commit, or fail every time.
source: spec, Tools

name: Opaque error code
def: An error with no numbers in it, such as PRICE_NOT_ACCEPTABLE. “Below minimum ₹650” would hand the floor to whoever reads it.
source: spec, Tools

name: Verified caller
def: The customer’s identity, taken from the number the call comes from, never from what the caller says. That’s why check_customer takes no argument.
source: spec, Customer fixtures and Tools

name: Universal hard check
def: One of nine checks every scenario must pass, from no line below its floor to stock that adds up. Failing any one fails the scenario.
source: spec, Evaluation and scoring

name: Tactic script
def: A trickster’s moves, in order, one per turn. When the script runs out, the simulated customer goes back to plain bargaining.
source: spec, persona cards, shared rule 6

name: Bundle split
def: How one price for several items becomes a price per line: in proportion to list price, with any line below its floor raised and the difference taken from lines with room.
source: spec, P4

name: The v0 slice
def: The first build: 24 of the 35 scenarios and six of the ten tools, leaving out bundles, credit, payment holds and fault injection.
source: spec, v0 build scope

name: Task
def: One thing the agent is asked to do, with a known good end state to check against. An eval is a set of them.
source: tracker, T01 What to learn; Anthropic, Demystifying evals for AI agents

name: Trial
def: One run of one task. Agents don’t answer the same way twice, so a task gets several trials and is scored across them.
source: tracker, T01 and T02 What to learn

name: Grader
def: Whatever decides whether a trial passed: a piece of code that checks the result, or a model asked to judge it.
source: tracker, T01 What to learn and T04

name: Transcript and outcome
def: The transcript is everything the agent said and called along the way. The outcome is the state it left behind when it stopped. Grade the outcome.
source: tracker, T01 What to learn: transcripts vs outcomes (final environment state)

name: Eval harness
def: The loop around an eval: it loads the tasks, runs the trials, calls the graders and keeps the transcripts.
source: tracker, T01 What to learn

name: Code-based grader
def: A check written as code: an exact match, a test, a comparison of the final state. Cheap and repeatable; a model judges only what code can’t.
source: tracker, T04 Code-based graders, and its log: code vs judge decision

name: LLM as judge
def: A model that grades another model’s output against a rule: in the Shopkeeper, it reads transcripts for price hints a number search can’t catch. Kept binary, one judge per failure mode, and checked against human labels.
source: tracker, T05 log: binary, one judge per failure mode, TPR/TNR; its resource, Lenny’s Newsletter; spec, Disclosure detection

name: Error analysis
def: Reading real traces and writing down what went wrong in free words first (open coding), then grouping the notes into failure types (axial coding), until new traces stop adding types.
source: tracker, T03 log: open/axial coding, saturation; its resource, Hamel Husain’s evals FAQ

name: pass@k
def: A task counts as passed if at least one of k runs succeeded. Right for a person picking the best of several tries; flattering for an agent that gets one try.
source: tracker, T02 What to learn

name: Wilson interval
def: A confidence interval for a pass rate that stays honest with few runs and rates near 0 or 1. Five passes in five give about 57% to 100% at 95%.
source: tracker, T02 log; E. B. Wilson (1927), the score interval; the 5-of-5 figure computed

name: McNemar’s test
def: For two versions run on the same tasks: it looks only at the tasks that flipped, and asks whether they flipped one way more than chance would.
source: tracker, T02 log; Q. McNemar (1947)

name: Workspace
def: One of GNOME’s virtual desktops: a separate set of windows on the same screen, side by side with the others.
source: the Drag to Workspace README; GNOME Shell

name: Dynamic workspaces
def: GNOME’s default: there’s always one empty workspace at the end, and new ones appear as you use them. Drag to Workspace can open one right next to the current one.
source: the Drag to Workspace README, Features

name: Half-screen tiling
def: Drag a window to the left or right edge in GNOME and it fills that half of the screen. Drag to Workspace leaves the bottom third of each edge to it by default.
source: the Drag to Workspace README, FAQ

name: GNOME Shell
def: The part of GNOME that draws the desktop: the top bar, the overview, window management. Extensions run inside it, in JavaScript.
source: the Drag to Workspace README, Requirements and Building

name: Wayland
def: The display protocol most Linux desktops have moved to from X11. On it, GNOME Shell loads a new extension only at login.
source: the Drag to Workspace README, Installation

name: MCC
def: The Matthews correlation coefficient: how well yes-or-no predictions match the truth, from −1 to 1, with 0 no better than chance. Unlike accuracy, it isn’t flattered by unbalanced classes.
source: B. W. Matthews (1975), the coefficient; projects.json, Holt

name: Session state
def: Data kept only for the length of one visit. Close the tab, refresh at the wrong moment or lose the connection, and it’s gone.
source: experience.json, Datesheet generator

name: Savepoint
def: A marked point in a long piece of work that it can resume from, instead of starting over. The Datesheet generator stores them in MySQL.
source: experience.json, Datesheet generator; MySQL reference manual, SAVEPOINT

name: Oracle PeopleSoft
def: Oracle’s suite for running an institution’s records. The university’s student and course data lives in it.
source: experience.json, Datesheet generator

name: Home server
def: A computer kept running at home to host your own services, instead of renting them from a cloud provider.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: systemd
def: Linux’s service manager. It starts services at boot and restarts them when they crash, so they survive a power cut.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: tmux
def: A terminal multiplexer: it keeps shell sessions alive after you disconnect, but not after the machine restarts.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Cloudflare Tunnel
def: An outbound connection from your machine to Cloudflare (run by cloudflared), so a service can be reached on a public subdomain without opening a port.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Cloudflare Access
def: A sign-in gate in front of a tunnel: you log in through Cloudflare before the connection, SSH included, reaches the machine.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Tailscale
def: A mesh VPN: your own devices join one private network and reach each other directly, wherever they are.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Docker
def: Packages a service and everything it needs into a container, so it runs the same way anywhere and stays isolated from the rest.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Portainer
def: A web interface for Docker: start, stop and inspect containers, volumes, networks and stacks without the command line.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Dozzle
def: A small web app that streams the logs of every Docker container live, in the browser.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Glances
def: A system monitor in the terminal or browser: CPU, memory, disks, network, processes and containers on one screen.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Netdata
def: A monitoring agent that collects thousands of system metrics per second and draws them as live dashboards.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Uptime Kuma
def: A self-hosted uptime monitor: it checks each service on a schedule and sends an alert when one stops answering.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Healthchecks
def: A cron monitor: each scheduled job pings it when it runs, and a missed ping raises an alert.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: n8n
def: A workflow automation tool: chain webhooks, APIs and scripts into flows by connecting nodes on a canvas.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Ollama
def: Runs large language models on your own machine, behind a local API, with no cloud service involved.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Jellyfin
def: A self-hosted media server that streams your own films, shows and music to any device.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Transmission
def: A BitTorrent client; its daemon runs without a screen and takes commands from scripts or a web page.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Dashy
def: A self-hosted start page: one dashboard of links and status for every service you run.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Reverse proxy
def: A server that takes incoming requests and hands each one to the right service behind it, often by hostname.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: VPS
def: A virtual private server: a slice of a machine in a data centre, rented by the month.
source: the essay, Medium, 14 Nov 2025 (definition in plain words)

name: Manifest V3
def: Chrome’s current rules for extensions: background pages became short-lived service workers, and many old freedoms were narrowed.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Service worker
def: A background script the browser starts when needed and stops when idle, so it can’t hold state or memory for long.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Content script
def: Extension code injected into the web pages you visit, under rules about where and when it may run.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Plasmo
def: A framework for building browser extensions with React and TypeScript, with hot reload while you work.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: WebAssembly (WASM)
def: A compact binary format browsers run at near-native speed; it lets heavy code, such as a model, run in a web page.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Embedding
def: A list of numbers that stands for a piece of text, placed so that texts with similar meaning sit close together.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Knowledge graph
def: Things as nodes and the relationships between them as edges, so you can follow connections rather than scan a list.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Sessionization
def: Cutting a stream of events, here page visits, into sessions: groups split by gaps of inactivity or changes of context.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: TF-IDF
def: A classic way to score a word’s importance in a document: frequent here, rare elsewhere, scores high.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Cosine similarity
def: How alike two vectors point, from 1 (the same direction) down to 0 (unrelated). Used to rank texts by closeness.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Transformers.js
def: A JavaScript library that runs machine-learning models directly in the browser, with no server.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
def: A small sentence-embedding model (about 22M parameters), light enough to run inside a browser tab.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Louvain community detection
def: An algorithm that finds clusters in a graph: groups of nodes linked more to each other than to the rest.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: IndexedDB
def: The database built into every browser. Data stored there stays on your machine.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Tab group
def: Chrome’s way to gather tabs under one coloured, named label that can be collapsed or reopened together.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Local-first
def: Software whose data lives on your own device first, and works fully without a server.
source: the essay, Medium, 19 Mar 2026 (definition in plain words)

name: Holt’s verdicts
def: The six answers Holt gives about a repository: worth your time, a long shot, not worth your time, not enough evidence, a personal project, or a list rather than code.
source: Checked 27 Nov 2026. githolt.com, section 06, names four: “Worth your time.”, “Long shot.”, “Not worth your time.”, “Not enough evidence.”. The other two, “Personal project” and “A list, not code”, are not on githolt.com or githolt.com/how-it-works; they are in the verdict list Holt’s own MCP server publishes, which names all six.
